place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 大比 · 半决 · 对马小宝
place.en: Chending Temple · The contest · The semi-final · Against Ma Xiaobao

setup.zh: 半决，在申时。对面是马小宝：一脸丹斑，练气五层，腰里挂着那面白衣人留下的铜镜。镜子要亮，得先喝他一口灵力，他脸上的斑要先红一下。「你跪下，叫三声爷爷，我便不照了。」
setup.en: The semi-final, mid-afternoon. Across from you, Ma Xiaobao: face blotched with pill-poison, Qi Refining layer five, at his waist the bronze mirror the man in white left behind. Before the mirror lights it must drink a mouthful of his power, and the blotches on his face flare first. "Kneel, call me grandpa three times, and I won't hold it up."

recap.zh: 半决，他的火弹叫你一层水气浇灭了。你不看镜子，看他的脸，斑一红就挪，躲一回念一笔公中的账，全外门跟着报数；他把你逼到台边，你按住胸口的木牌，掌心托着自拍镜，把最后那一道光原样扔了回去。两面镜子都裂了，马小宝叫自己的镜子喝干，栽在台上；他爹在船头上转过了身。
recap.en: In the semi-final a film of water mist put out his fire bolt. You watched not the mirror but his face, moved whenever the blotches flared, read out a line of the common-fund account at every dodge, and the whole outer court counted along; he drove you to the edge, you pressed the token on your chest and, the selfie mirror on your palm, threw the last beam straight back. Both mirrors cracked; drunk dry by his own mirror, Ma Xiaobao pitched onto the stage; on the boat's bow his father turned away.

zh: 申时，半决。对面，马小宝。一面认东西的铜镜。
en: Mid-afternoon, the semi-final. Across from you, Ma Xiaobao. A bronze mirror that recognises things.
Don't watch the mirror. Watch his face.

story.zh:
小满心里慢慢地算了一笔账。昨天夜里，马小宝拿镜子照铺，没往里灌灵力，镜子上只有火光，木牌都烫成那样；今天灌了灵力，照上胸口，便不是烫一烫的事了。光是躲不掉的，镜面一亮，光就到了。可那镜子只照它对着的地方，马小宝两手捧着它，捧在身前；镜子要亮，得先喝一口马小宝的灵力，他脸上的斑，要先红一下。上午照鲁泥鳅，已经喝了三口；一夜吞上去的两层，是虚的，经不起它喝几口。他想：那就不看镜子，看他的脸。斑一红，就挪，挪到镜子对不着的地方去，让他转身，让他追，让他一口一口地喝——喝到只剩最后一口，最后那一口，拿镜子接。

拿镜子接，便是拿饭桶昨夜吐出来的那面自拍镜去接。蜡烛的光打上去，它原样扔回来；马小宝那面镜子喝的是人，吐的是什么光，它扔不扔得回去，他不知道。他只知道，不接，那道光便照进木牌里去。

半决赛在申时。另一个半边，是祁长松对内门那个七层；这一个半边，是他对马小宝。

小满往台上走的时候，阿禾挤过来，一把拽住他那条左臂，拆了上头那圈浸透了的布条，换上一条干净的，一圈一圈缠得极紧，勒得他咧嘴。她的手按在伤口上，按了好一会儿，按得久了些。小满觉出那块地方一凉，跟着一暖，像开春头一场雨落进了干地里——血不往外渗了，那条胳膊攥得起拳头了。她袖口底下透出一点青，像柳梢上一点新芽，只一霎，便叫袖子盖住了；台下两百来双眼睛，都看着台上。她脸上一点颜色也没有，塞给他半块烙饼，硬得像一块瓦：「垫垫肚子。空着肚子挨揍，更疼。」他把饼揣进怀里，贴着木牌。

马小宝站在台上，腰里那面铜镜给日头一照，亮得晃眼。他冲台下团团一拱手，扯着嗓子道：「诸位！我这面镜子，是太华山太一宫下来的白衣仙长亲手留给我爹的，能照妖，能退敌，还能照见人心。今天，当着全观，我拿它照一照——」他拿镜子一指小满，「——一个五行杂灵根，四层，把内门的卢师兄扔下了台，把秦师姐也打了下去，是人，是妖？」台下哄的一声，笑的，嚷的，起哄的，搅成一片。

马小宝又道：「沈小满。你跪下，叫三声爷爷，我便不照了，让你自己走下去。」台下有人起哄：「跪！跪！」一声接一声，起哄的人越来越多，喊到后来，竟有了节拍。便在这一片「跪」声里，人群当中忽然冒出一个嗓子，又尖又哑，破得像一面裂了的锣：「别跪——！」众人回头一看，是孙二狗。他下巴上贴着膏药，右手缠成一个白布包，站在人堆里，比旁人高出半个头，脸涨得通红。四下里一愣，跟着便哄笑起来：「二狗！你一个输了的，喊什么！」孙二狗的脸红到了耳朵根，可他没有坐下，也没有缩回去，就那么直挺挺地站着。

小满站在台上，看着马小宝。他想起那一年，马小宝站在他家门口，手里捏着桂花糕，叫他学声狗叫，给他舔一口。他没有说出来。马小宝凑近了一步，声音压得只有台上两个人听得见：「凶崖上，你听见了。你在墙里头喘气，我也听见了。」他左手一甩，甩出一颗火弹，又大又歪，带着一股丹药的焦糊味；小满抬手一根冰锥迎上去，「嗤」的一声，火弹灭在半道上，冰锥也化成了一股白烟。马小宝咬咬牙，把镜子从腰里扯了下来。
story.en:
Xiaoman worked out a sum, slowly. Last night Ma Xiaobao had swept the bunks with that mirror without pouring any power into it — nothing on it but firelight, and still the token had burned like that; today, with power poured in, landing on his chest, it wouldn't stop at burning. Light can't be dodged; the moment the mirror's face lights, the light is there. But the mirror only shines where it points, and Ma Xiaobao held it in both hands, in front of him; and before the mirror could light it had to drink a mouthful of Ma Xiaobao's power — the blotches on his face would flare first. On Lu this morning it had drunk three mouthfuls already; two layers swallowed in a night were hollow, they couldn't stand many more. Then don't watch the mirror, he thought; watch his face. When the blotches flare, move — move where the mirror can't point, make him turn, make him chase, let him drink mouthful after mouthful — till he's down to the last one, and that last one, catch with a mirror.

Catch it with a mirror meant catch it with the selfie mirror the Tub had spat out last night. Candlelight struck it and it threw the light straight back; Ma Xiaobao's mirror drank a man, and whether it could throw back whatever light that spat out, he didn't know. He only knew that if he didn't catch it, the light would go into the token.

The semi-finals were at the hour of Shen, mid-afternoon. In the other half, Qi Changsong against the inner-court layer seven; in this half, him against Ma Xiaobao.

As Xiaoman went up to the stage, A He squeezed over, caught hold of his left arm, unwound the soaked strip of cloth, and bound on a clean one, turn after turn, so tight he grimaced. Her hand stayed pressed on the wound a good while — a little too long. Xiaoman felt the place go cool, then warm, like the first spring rain falling into dry ground — the blood stopped seeping, and the arm could close into a fist. Under her cuff showed a touch of green, like a new bud on a willow tip, one instant, then the sleeve covered it; the two hundred-odd pairs of eyes below were all on the stage. There wasn't a drop of colour in her face. She pushed half a flatbread at him, hard as a roof tile: "Line your stomach. A beating on an empty stomach hurts more." He tucked the bread into his coat, against the token.

Ma Xiaobao stood on the stage, the bronze mirror at his waist dazzling in the sun. He cupped his fists all round and bawled: "Everyone! This mirror an immortal in white, down from the Taiyi Palace on Mount Taihua, left with my father with his own hands — it shows demons, repels enemies, and shows the heart. Today, before the whole temple, I'll hold it up to —" he pointed it at Xiaoman, "— a five-element mixed root, layer four, who threw Brother Lu of the inner court off the stage and knocked Sister Qin down too. Man, or demon?" The crowd erupted — laughing, shouting, egging on, all in a jumble.

"Shen Xiaoman," said Ma Xiaobao, "kneel, call me grandpa three times, and I won't hold it up; I'll let you walk down yourself." Someone below started up: "Kneel! Kneel!" Again and again, more and more of them, till it took on a beat. And in the middle of the chanting a voice rose from the crowd, shrill and hoarse, cracked like a split gong: "Don't kneel —!" Everyone turned: Sun Ergou, a plaster on his chin, his right hand bound into a white lump, half a head above the crowd, face flushed dark. A pause, then laughter: "Ergou! You lost, what are you yelling for!" Sun Ergou went red to the ears, but he didn't sit down and he didn't shrink back; he just stood there, straight.

Xiaoman stood on the stage and looked at Ma Xiaobao. He remembered that year, Ma Xiaobao at their door with an osmanthus cake, telling him to bark like a dog and he'd get a lick. He didn't say it. Ma Xiaobao came a step closer, his voice so low only the two of them on the stage could hear: "On the Cliff of Danger — you heard. You were breathing inside the wall, and I heard you too." His left hand flung out a fire bolt, big and lopsided, reeking of scorched pills; Xiaoman raised a hand and sent an ice spike to meet it — hiss — and the bolt died halfway, the spike gone to a puff of white smoke with it. Ma Xiaobao gritted his teeth and tore the mirror off his belt.

label.en: Watch his face; read out the common fund

exits.means: fights Ma Xiaobao: moves whenever the blotches flare, reads the common-fund account at every dodge, and at the edge catches the mirror's last beam in his palm

withdrawn.zh: 马小宝的铜镜又亮了，他笑得更开心了。——再来。
withdrawn.en: Ma Xiaobao's mirror flashes again, and he smiles even wider. — Again.

story.zh:
他两手捧起镜子。小满不看镜子，看他的脸。那脸上的斑「腾」地一红——小满已经往左边挪了两步，挪到了马小宝的右手边上。镜面这才一亮，一道黄光扑在他方才站的那块青石板上，石缝里的草登时白了一片。马小宝咬着牙，捧着镜子往右转。他吞了一夜的丹，身子是沉的，转得慢；他转过来，斑一红，小满又挪了，挪到了他的背后。小满落了地，开口道：「九月初十，公中，一块。」马小宝一愣，又转身，又照，照了个空：「十月初一，一块。」又转，又照：「冬月初一，两块。因由：畜生也要吃饭。」台下有人「噗」地笑出了声。马小宝咬着牙再照，他再挪：「腊月初一，两块。」一笔一笔，日子、数目，张口就来，一个也不错。

人堆里忽然有人跟着喊了一嗓子，又尖又哑：「九月初十，我也一块！」是孙二狗。跟着便是第二个：「我两块！」第三个：「我也两块——他说我夜里打呼！」台下「哈哈哈」笑倒了一片。外门一百多号人，一个月一个月往那只描金匣子里交的，谁心里没有一本账？方才喊「跪」的那拨人，这时候一个接一个，报的全是数，报到后来，竟也有了节拍。台北面竹椅上，观主拢着手，没有动；周衡站在他身后，翻开了账簿，提起笔，记了一行。马小宝的表伯在台角咳了一声，又咳了一声，咳得谁也没理他。马小宝每照一回，脸上的斑便鼓一回，红一回，捧镜子的手一回比一回抖，喘气一口比一口粗。他站住了，咬着牙道：「躲？你就会躲？」小满没有答。

马小宝喘着，往山脚下泗水那边望了一眼。船头上那个宽得像门的人，站起来了，正望着这边。马小宝的脸白了一白，斑却红得更凶了。他不照了。他捧着镜子，一步一步往前逼，不让小满再绕到他身后去；小满往左，他往左，小满往右，他往右，一步一步，把小满逼到了台边。小满脚后跟底下，又只剩了半寸。左边是马小宝的镜子，右边是马小宝的镜子，身后是冻土。马小宝那张脸上，斑一片挨一片，红得发紫，他把身子里剩下的那一口，全灌进了镜子里。

那一霎，小满胸口的木牌烫得像一块烧红的铁。躲了五道，等的就是这一道。他没处挪了。他把左手平平地按在胸口上，压住了那块木牌，右手从袖子里摸出那面自拍镜，托在掌心里，镜面朝外，迎了上去——巴掌大一块铜，缺着一个角。台下有人「噗」地笑出了声：「他也有镜子？」

那一道黄光撞在了自拍镜上。它不像打在青石板上那样一扑就散，倒像一根冰锥，往镜子里钻，钻着找什么东西——找木牌，找木牌里那一缕银。自拍镜不认得它。这面破铜一辈子只会一样：什么光打上来，原样扔回去。「嗡」的一声，那道黄光折了回去，正扑在马小宝自己的镜面上。马小宝那面镜子认得自己的光，张嘴便喝——喝的是捧镜子的人。他脸上的斑「腾」地紫了，身子里剩的那一口，叫自己的镜子一口一口往外抽，抽出来照过去，又叫自拍镜扔回来；两面镜子当中，拉成了一根亮得睁不开眼的光柱。小满掌心里那块铜烫得托不住，他没撒手——五扇门一齐开了，头一回，在人前扒开了；五行那一圈在他身子里转成了一个轮子，转得飞快，全推到那一只手掌上，托着它。他按着胸口的那只手底下，那块木牌隔着衣裳亮了一亮，一线银光从他指缝里漏出来，只一霎，便灭了。马小宝手里的镜子先是「嗡」的一声，跟着「咔」的一响，镜面上从当中裂开一道缝，裂缝一路爬到镜沿，镜子里的光，灭了。跟着又是「咔」的一声——小满掌心里那面自拍镜，从缺角那里裂开了，碎成七八瓣，叮叮当当掉在青石板上。碎的那一霎，最后一缕光从裂缝里漏了下去，漏进了他的掌心，凉得像一根针。

演武场上，一个声音也没有。

那一霎，有没有人看见他指缝里那一线银，小满不知道。他只听见自己的心，一下一下，撞着胸口那块木牌。

马小宝举着那面裂了的铜镜，傻站在台上。他把镜子翻过来看看，又翻过去看看，使劲拍了两下。然后他的腿一软，跪了下去，跟着整个人往前一栽，脸贴在青石板上，不动了。身子里那点虚灵力，早叫他自己那面镜子喝干了，像一口破缸，外头看着满，底下全是裂缝。

小满站在台边，没有再出手。他蹲下来，看着那张贴在石头上的脸，满脸的斑，嘴唇发白，喘得像一条搁在岸上的鱼。他低声道：「那些，是公中的。还有一笔，不在公中——冬月初二夜，凶崖，孟有田。」马小宝的眼珠子动了一动，没有看他，越过他的肩膀，往山门外头泗水那边望。山脚下，马家那条船还泊着，船头上站着那个宽得像门的人，望着这边，望了一会儿，转过身去，钻进了船舱。

马小宝的眼睛还望着那条船，望得像一个在集上走丢了的孩子。小满蹲在那里，把到了嘴边的下一句，咽了回去。
story.en:
He held it up in both hands. Xiaoman didn't watch the mirror; he watched his face. The blotches flared red — and Xiaoman had already moved two steps left, round to Ma Xiaobao's right hand. Only then did the mirror light, and a beam of yellow light struck the slab where he had just stood; the grass in the crack went white at once. Ma Xiaobao gritted his teeth and turned right with the mirror. He had swallowed a night's worth of pills and his body was heavy; he turned slowly; when he came round, the blotches flared, and Xiaoman moved again, round behind him. Xiaoman landed and said: "Tenth of the ninth month, common fund, one stone." Ma Xiaobao faltered, turned, flashed, hit nothing: "First of the tenth, one." Turned again, flashed again: "First of the eleventh, two. Reason: the animal has to eat too." Someone below snorted out a laugh. Ma Xiaobao gritted his teeth and flashed again; he moved again: "First of the twelfth, two." Line by line, dates and sums, out of his mouth without a pause, not one wrong.

Out of the crowd someone suddenly shouted along, shrill and hoarse: "Tenth of the ninth, me too, one!" Sun Ergou. Then a second: "Me, two!" A third: "Me too, two — he said I snore!" A whole stretch of the crowd fell over laughing — "Hahaha!" A hundred-odd in the outer court, month after month into that gilt box — who didn't carry an account in his head? The same lot who had chanted "kneel" now called out one after another, nothing but numbers, until the numbers too took on a beat. In the bamboo chair north of the stage the abbot sat with his hands in his sleeves and didn't move; behind him Zhou Heng opened his ledger, lifted his brush, and wrote a line. Ma Xiaobao's great-uncle coughed at the corner of the stage, coughed again, and nobody paid him any mind. Every flash, the blotches on Ma Xiaobao's face swelled and flared, the hands holding the mirror shook worse, and each breath came coarser than the last. He stopped and said through his teeth: "Dodge? Is that all you can do?" Xiaoman didn't answer.

Panting, Ma Xiaobao glanced down the mountain toward the Si. On the boat's bow the man as broad as a door had stood up and was watching. Ma Xiaobao's face went a shade whiter, and the blotches burned redder still. He stopped flashing. Holding the mirror he pressed forward step by step, so Xiaoman couldn't get round behind him again; Xiaoman went left, he went left; Xiaoman went right, he went right; step by step he drove Xiaoman to the edge. Under Xiaoman's heels, half an inch again. Left, Ma Xiaobao's mirror; right, Ma Xiaobao's mirror; behind, frozen earth. On Ma Xiaobao's face the blotches lay patch on patch, red going purple, and he poured the last mouthful left in him into the mirror.

In that instant the token on Xiaoman's chest burned like red-hot iron. Five beams dodged; this was the one he had waited for. He had nowhere left to move. He laid his left hand flat on his chest, pressing the token down, took the selfie mirror out of his sleeve with his right, held it on his palm face outward, and met the light with it — a palm's breadth of bronze with a corner chipped off. Someone below snorted with laughter: "He's got a mirror too?"

The yellow beam struck the selfie mirror. It didn't scatter the way it had on the bluestone; it was like an icicle boring into the mirror, boring and searching for something — for the token, for the one wisp of silver inside it. The selfie mirror didn't know it. All its life this scrap of bronze could do one thing: whatever light struck it, it threw straight back. *Hmmm* — the yellow beam bent back and landed full on the face of Ma Xiaobao's own mirror. Ma Xiaobao's mirror knew its own light and opened its mouth to drink — and what it drank was the man holding it. The blotches on his face flared purple; the last mouthful in him was pulled out, sip by sip, by his own mirror, pulled out and shone across and thrown back again by the selfie mirror; between the two mirrors stretched a pillar of light too bright to look at. The bronze in Xiaoman's palm burned too hot to hold; he didn't let go — all five of his doors opened at once, raked open for the first time in front of everyone; the round of the five elements spun in him like a wheel, fast, and he pushed all of it into that one palm, holding the mirror up. Under the hand pressed to his chest the token glowed once through his clothes, and a thread of silver light leaked out between his fingers — one instant, then gone. In Ma Xiaobao's hands the mirror first went *hmmm*, then *crack*: a split opened across the middle of its face and crawled out to the rim, and the light in the mirror went out. Then another *crack* — the selfie mirror in Xiaoman's palm split from its chipped corner and broke into seven or eight pieces that tinkled down onto the bluestone. In the instant it broke, the last thread of light leaked through the crack and into his palm, cold as a needle.

On the training ground, not a sound.

Whether anyone in that instant saw the thread of silver between his fingers, Xiaoman didn't know. He heard only his own heart, beat by beat, knocking against the token on his chest.

Ma Xiaobao stood there with the cracked bronze mirror up, dumbfounded. He turned it over and back again and slapped it twice. Then his legs gave, he dropped to his knees, and the whole of him pitched forward, his face against the bluestone, and didn't move. The hollow power in him his own mirror had long since drunk dry — like a broken vat, full to look at from outside, all cracks at the bottom.

Xiaoman stood at the edge and struck no more. He crouched and looked at the face pressed to the stone, all blotches, lips white, gasping like a fish left on the bank. He said low: "Those are the common fund's. There's one more, not in the common fund — second night of the eleventh month, the Cliff of Danger, Meng Youtian." Ma Xiaobao's eyes moved, but didn't look at him; they went past his shoulder, out beyond the gate toward the Si. Down at the foot of the mountain the Ma boat was still moored, the man as broad as a door standing in the bow, looking this way; he looked a while, then turned and ducked into the cabin.

Ma Xiaobao's eyes were still on the boat, staring like a child lost at a fair. Crouching there, Xiaoman swallowed the next thing he had been about to say.
